correctness.rationale: In oriented incidence convention a negative signed-line edge is a directed two-step path. Every odd cycle requires a mixed vertex, incurring at least min degree minus one. Vertex-disjointness permits summing bounds. The block-cut tree propagates pure sources/sinks and designated single mixed vertices to attain equality. Equality forces one minimum-degree mixed vertex per odd cycle. For each such selection, a global binary orientation phase and independently one extra binary choice at every selected vertex with attached noncycle edges enumerate all optimal orientations. Connectivity of the ordinary line graph makes global reversal the exact two-to-one kernel, so the formula counts labeled signed assignments. Empty-graph exception treated. The actual package script separately enumerates orientation costs and switchings on 5,428 small instances and additional random cacti, all agreeing.

The earlier Belardo–Stanić–Zaslavsky signed-line paper provides different generic frustration inequalities. Literature and indexed research searches for exact equivalences, broader dominance, tabulations and implications did not identify coverage. In particular an unevaluated general min-over-orientations identity is not an exact cactus formula and gives no optimal signature count. Equivalent results may remain undiscovered.

value.rationale: Natural disjoint-cycle cactus class includes arbitrary numbers of odd cycles connected by bridges and arbitrary pendant trees, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice. Exact frustration depends on minimum *ambient degrees* on odd cycles and can grow without bound even while edge-bipartization defect remains one (uniform odd suns). The second exact formula gives the entire optimal signature degeneracy and diagnoses a phase change at minimum cycle degree two. This provides structural and enumerative information not furnished by the general orientation min identity or usual bounds.
